question: A 24-year-old woman presents with secondary amenorrhea following a D&C for missed abortion 6 months ago. Serum FSH, LH, and oestradiol are all NORMAL. Progesterone challenge test produces NO withdrawal bleed. What is the most likely diagnosis?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: POI shows elevated FSH and LH (hypergonadotrophic hypogonadism) because the ovaries are failing and the pituitary is signalling maximally. Here, FSH and LH are normal.
Hypothalamic amenorrhea shows low FSH/LH (hypogonadotrophic) due to GnRH pulse suppression. Normal hormone levels and a preceding uterine procedure point elsewhere.

Correct. Secondary amenorrhea after uterine instrumentation + normal hormone levels + absent progesterone withdrawal = Asherman syndrome. The endometrial cavity is obliterated by adhesions; the ovaries are functioning normally but there is no endometrium to shed.

Prolactinoma causes hypogonadotrophic hypogonadism via hyperprolactinaemia suppressing GnRH. A prolactin level would be elevated. Normal FSH/LH and the post-instrumentation history make Asherman far more likely.

overallFeedback.feedback: Key logic: normal FSH+LH+E2 = normal ovarian function. Absent withdrawal bleed despite normal oestrogen = outflow tract/uterine problem. Post-D&C context = Asherman syndrome (intrauterine adhesions).

Correct. The triad of: (1) uterine instrumentation history, (2) normal HPO axis hormones, and (3) absent progesterone withdrawal bleed = Asherman syndrome until proven otherwise. Confirm with hysteroscopy.
